newsitem.title: FRANCE: French deputy cites fraud in mad cow feed imports.
newsitem.headline: French deputy cites fraud in mad cow feed imports.

text.p: A leading figure in a French parliamentary probe into mad cow disease said on Tuesday that suspect animal feed had reached France fraudulently in the 1980s but dismissed a report that Belgium would be held to blame.

Jean-Francois Mattei, author of an unpublished report on the findings of a committee set up by the lower National Assembly, said imports of feed containing bonemeal into France in the late 1980s were still shrouded in mystery.

"Today we are totally unable to assess the reality and the scope of bonemeal imports during the critical period. This means that we clearly think there has been fraud," Mattei told reporters after the panel adopted his report with amendments.
The French newspaper Le Monde reported on Tuesday that Mattei's draft report had cited evidence that suspect, relabelled British feed may have been imported into France through Belgium.

It said the report seriously examined the suggestion that Belgium was a "hub for the movement of British bonemeal trying to lose its identity" from 1988 onwards. It said there may have been a "laundering circuit for British bonemeal, which was systematically relabelled as coming from Ireland".
But Mattei said the report to be published on January 21 would not contain such an accusation and said the question of a Belgian hub for laundering feed had never been discussed.
"You won't find a trace of this in the report," he said.
Matttei, a pariamentary deputy for the government's junior UDF coalition party, did not say how the suspected fraud worked.

The recycling of animal parts such as bonemeal into feed is the main suspected cause of the spread of the disease, bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), to thousands of British cattle from the 1980s onwards.
Britain prompted a Europe-wide health scare last year by announcing that infected beef might also cause the fatal brain disorder Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD) in humans.
France banned imports of the British feed in 1989.
Mattei said the committee's report would however recount evidence of a lack of coordination between French authorities and call for a new, independent safety body to be set up.
"It is totally obvious this is the opportunity to stress the need for our country to have a health security agency," he said.

He also gave a strong hint that the report would criticise the handling of the disease on a a European scale -- the second such report to do so this month. "At European level, economic interest superseded public health," Mattei said.

A draft European Parliament report leaked last week attacked both Britain and the European Union's Brussels headquarters for bungling their response to BSE. France in turn has accused other EU nations of mishandling their role in containing the crisis.
France reported its 26th case of BSE on Monday.
